amulet.somdej.name: Phra Somdej
amulet.somdej.desc: A cream-white votive tablet, pressed from temple powder. The venerable's calm settles over whoever carries it with respect.
amulet.takrut.name: Takrut
amulet.takrut.desc: A little scroll of yantra script rolled in metal, worn on a cord. What is written inside is not for reading — it is for keeping you out of harm's path.
amulet.sing.name: Sing Amulet
amulet.sing.desc: A carved lion, jaw set, sitting proud. Carry it and your heart remembers it has teeth too.
amulet.paladkhik.name: Palad Khik
amulet.paladkhik.desc: A small carved charm of a shape best kept in the pocket, na. Good things find their way to the one who carries it. Do not show granny.
amulet.nangkwak.name: Nang Kwak
amulet.nangkwak.desc: The beckoning lady, hand raised, calling customers and coin the way one calls a cat. Shopkeepers swear by her. She takes no salary — only respect.
amulet.jingjok.name: Jing-jok Charm
amulet.jingjok.desc: A little house gecko in pale jade. Geckos speak before things happen — this one whispers about tomorrow, if you listen.
omen.coucal: A coucal called from the west at first light. The old people smile at that.
omen.housegecko: A house gecko chirped an odd number of times over the door. Lucky number, they say.
omen.almsround: You woke in time to see the monks pass on alms round. A good start follows a good start.
omen.lottery: You dreamt of numbers, clear as day. Somebody should hold something lucky today.
omen.firstsale: The first customer of the morning paid without haggling. Merchants call that a blessed till.
omen.teeth: You dreamt your teeth came loose. The old people say to walk carefully after that dream.
omen.owl: An owl cried on the roof last night. Best keep protection close today.
omen.ricepot: The rice pot boiled over this morning. A day for a careful hand and a beckoning charm.
omen.dogs: The soi dogs howled at nothing before dawn. Whatever they saw, better to face the day with courage.
omen.resting: The old aunties advise: today is a resting day for charms. Let them sleep in the pocket — showing them off today helps nobody.
omen.buffdesc: Dawn omens, read the Chiang Mai way. The right amulet can answer them.
wear.none: You tuck every charm safely into your pocket.
wear.some: You put on the {{name}}. It settles warm against your chest.
nangkwak.tip: A stranger pressed {{amount}}g into your hand. Nang Kwak beckons, customers come.
menu.title: Charms of Chiang Mai — today's reading
menu.footer: Press 1-6 to wear a charm · 0 to tuck them all away · Esc to close
menu.empty: No amulets yet. Lung Saeng sets up at the bus stop on market days — looking is free, na.
seller.name: Lung Saeng
seller.arrived: Lung Saeng the amulet seller has set out his tray at the bus stop.
seller.greet.1: Oh, farmer! Come, come. Looking is free. Protection — small price, na.$h
seller.greet.2: Good day for you, good day for me. My charms all wake up blessed already — you only bring the money part.$h
seller.greet.3: You look tired, na. Work hard is good, but luck works harder. I give farmer price, cannot go lower — my cousin blesses these himself.
seller.greet.4: Same same as last time, but different. New moon, new blessings. You need, I have. You no need — you still maybe have, safer that way, na?$h
